clue.text: Food for cooking dinner gets prepared after one

indicators.note: after tells us the rearranged letters follow the numeral rather than precede it

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been chopped and mixed, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone checks what goes into the meal before tonight's dinner is cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingredients are the raw items that a recipe combines, the things a cook works with.

clue.text: Green note

definitions.meaning: first meaning: unprocessed, environmentally friendly, organic
second meaning: in music, a note that is neither sharp nor flat

explanation.walkthrough: Green looks like a colour, but here it is the eco sense; note is the musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Products sold as green or eco-friendly are described as wholesome and unadulterated; in notation the sign cancelling a sharp or flat names a plain tone.

clue.text: Fragrant liquid so rare and wet, splashed around

indicators.note: liquid splashed around is scattered everywhere, so the letters before it end up in a new order

parts.note: the words so, rare and wet, joined by and, which supplies no letters

explanation.surface: Someone describes an unusual perfume being sprinkled about.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a scented water distilled from petals, used in perfumery and in sweets such as Turkish delight.

clue.text: Cash: bread, though not ready?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the mixture of flour and water before baking, bread not yet ready to eat

explanation.walkthrough: Bread is itself slang for money, so the clue looks like two words for cash; the question mark flags the baking sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for money and also names raw, unbaked mixture of flour, yeast and water.

clue.text: Shops all opening, eight million people outside running in, apparently

indicators.note: all opening means every word gives up its opening, so only the first letter of each following word counts

parts.words: eight million people outside running in, apparently
parts.note: the first letters of these seven words, read in order

explanation.surface: Stores throw open their doors as a city's eight million residents queue outside and then rush in.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a sales-day news report; the whole tail of the clue is just a string of initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large store, a grand word for a shop, and the Latin plural ends in -ia.

clue.text: Pilot I suspect circling right capital city

indicators.note: circling means going round something, so the mixed letters surround the next piece
suspect as an adjective means dubious or not genuine, so the letters are not in their true order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An aviator, under suspicion, flies in circles above a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital of Libya, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Unproven belief in fresh start under leader in parliament

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below, so the fresh start comes second
the leader of a word is its first letter, so only the start of the following word is kept

parts.note: first letter of parliament
a fresh start is a resumption, starting again after a break

explanation.surface: A political party leader promises a fresh start under their leadership in parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A presumption is something assumed to be true without proof, an assumption taken for granted.

clue.text: Leave property on Monopoly board

definitions.meaning: first meaning: abandon someone somewhere with no way out
second meaning: a red square on the London edition of the board game, named after a street in central London

explanation.walkthrough: The London Monopoly board has a street called this, coloured red next to Fleet Street and Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone helpless is to abandon them, as a ship left on a beach; separately, the London street appears as a purchasable square in the game.

clue.text: In reverse, place a rock in wheels

indicators.note: in reverse means going backwards, so the whole string is read from the end

parts.note: to place something is to set it down
taken as written
a tor is a rocky outcrop on a hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone backs a vehicle up to set a stone among its wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: Wheels looks like a noun among the wheels of a car, but it is the verb at the end of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that wheels turns round on an axis or pivot, which is what spinning objects do.

clue.text: One visiting a French apartment, due

parts.note: un is the French word for a

indicators.note: someone visiting goes inside a home, so this letter goes into the dwelling

parts.note: pad is slang for a flat or apartment
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A guest stays at a Parisian flat on which the rent is owing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that is due has not been settled yet, so it remains outstanding.

clue.text: Communist playing knotty roles

indicators.note: playing suggests acting out parts or fooling about, so the letters take up new positions

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor takes on tricky parts as a left-wing revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Trotsky was a leading Bolshevik revolutionary, founder of the Red Army, and an example of a Marxist.

clue.text: Bird in queue behind rail

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the queue word follows the rail word

parts.note: a spar is a pole or bar, like a rail
a row is a line of people or things

explanation.surface: A bird perches in a line behind a fence rail.
explanation.definitionFit: The house sparrow is a small brown songbird, one of the commonest birds in towns.

clue.text: Tailless insect absorbs second bodily substance

indicators.note: absorbing means taking something in, so the shortened insect holds the next piece
without a tail means the final letter of the creature is dropped

parts.note: a hornet is a large wasp
mo is short for moment, a second

explanation.surface: A stingless wasp soaks up a second dose of something the body produces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hormones such as insulin and adrenaline are chemical messengers made by glands and carried in the blood.

clue.text: Gong banged finally, dinner say brought round?

indicators.note: brought round means wrapped around something, so the meal word encloses the kept letter

parts.note: dinner is an example of a meal, which say signals

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of banged

explanation.surface: A gong is struck at the end, announcing that dinner is served.
explanation.walkthrough: Gong looks like the dinner gong in the surface, but it is British slang for a medal or award.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a gong is a decoration or honour awarded to someone.

clue.text: Islander, like chap I dressed in brown

indicators.note: to be dressed in something is to be wrapped in it, so the first words sit inside the colour

parts.note: tan is a light brown
as means like, in comparisons
a chap is a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes an island dweller as a fellow just like them, clad in brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is the island state south of mainland Australia, so a native of it is an islander.

clue.text: 'Ass' infers stupid type

indicators.note: something stupid is muddled, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone concludes that a person called an ass must be a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Type looks like a kind of person, but it means printing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This names a style of typeface, lettering without the small strokes finishing each character.

clue.text: Incompetent Dan put in, opener finally trapped in cricket game

indicators.note: incompetent work is badly done, so the letters are put together wrongly
trapped in says the kept letter is caught among the other letters being mixed

parts.note: the main letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: finally keeps only the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of opener

explanation.surface: A useless player named Dan is sent in to bat, and the opening batsman is stuck in a cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an informal form of cricket in which the batter must run every time the ball is hit.

clue.text: Uriah upset about Victor is grumpy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the turned name goes round the next pieces
upset means turned over, and in a down clue that reads the name from bottom to top

parts.note: Uriah Heep is the fawning clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield
V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Uriah is annoyed about someone called Victor, who is in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah is the Dickens villain, so it stands for his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone grumpy is irritable and easily annoyed, sulky and bad-tempered.

clue.text: Wandering casually initially, I had a day going uphill

indicators.note: in a down clue, going uphill means reading from bottom to top
initially points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of casually
I'd is short for I had
taken as written
Mon is short for Monday

explanation.surface: A hiker recalls a relaxed day spent strolling up a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomads move from place to place without a fixed home, roaming with their herds.

clue.text: Gift first of lemons in yellow

indicators.note: in places the kept letter inside the colour word

parts.note: fair hair is light or blond, a yellowish colour

indicators.note: first of keeps just the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: first letter of lemons

explanation.surface: A present of a lemon, wrapped in yellow paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift can mean a natural talent, and having a knack for something is the same idea.

clue.text: Back African party, well on the fringes

indicators.note: fringes are edges, so the second word forms the border around the party

parts.note: fine means well, in good health
the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: Support an African political party that is doing well at the margins.
explanation.walkthrough: Back looks like a direction, but it is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a project is to fund it, providing the money it needs.

clue.text: Ask a page to put on ring

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on means placed on top, so the first pieces stand above the ring word

parts.note: taken as written
p is the abbreviation for page
bells ring out in a peal

explanation.surface: Someone asks a young attendant to wear a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a plea is to request something earnestly, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Employ too many staff, thousand in Verona, surprisingly

indicators.note: in puts the thousand inside the mixed city
something that happens surprisingly is out of the expected order, so the city's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: An Italian business in Verona has hired a thousand workers, far more than it needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Overmanning means a workforce larger than the job needs, too many hands on payroll.

clue.text: Relative in fleece instantly turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upwards
in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of fleece and the start of instantly

explanation.surface: A family member wearing a fleece appears at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Your brother's or sister's daughter is a family member of yours.

clue.text: Eject bags with shallow box

indicators.note: to bag something is to capture it, so the first word holds the next

parts.note: to spit is to eject from the mouth
and means with, along with

explanation.surface: Someone throws out sacks along with a shallow crate.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's play area filled with sand is often a low wooden frame in a garden or playground.

clue.text: Fill puzzle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pierce all over, as in a target full of bullet holes
second meaning: a conundrum or enigma

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense comes from the coarse sieve full of holes, as in bullets peppering a target.
explanation.definitionFit: To pepper something with holes means to permeate it thoroughly, and a conundrum or enigma is a question posed as a game.

clue.text: Made off with bag — loot!

parts.note: ran off means made off, fled
a sack is a large bag

explanation.surface: A thief escapes carrying a sack, shouting about the plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunder a place is to search it violently and steal its contents.

clue.text: Very little grain?

parts.note: surface reading: a tiny amount, an insignificant sum of money
setter's reading: grain scattered for farmyard poultry

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom for a trivial amount of money, and literally the corn thrown to hens.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a paltry sum, while literally naming what poultry eat.
